purpose: User-directed investigation, not profile-driven: (1) whether any try/catch in PictTag.PgfCodec blocks JIT inlining of a genuinely hot method, and whether restructuring could recover that inlining; (2) whether forcing inlining via [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] on small, extremely-hot leaf methods that currently lack it improves the managed decode benchmark.

part1_tryCatchAudit.method: grep for every `try`/`catch`/`finally` occurrence across source/PictTag.PgfCodec/*.cs.
part1_tryCatchAudit.finding: Exception handling appears in exactly 3 files: PgfDecodeSession.cs (TryOpen's header-parse try/catch, DecodeOneLevel's per-level try/catch, DecodeOneLevelRoi's per-level try/catch, TryDecode's rent/return try/finally), PgfImageDecoder.cs (TryDecode's rent/return try/finally), and PgfProgressiveDecoder.cs (its own rent/return try/finally). Every one of these wraps a large, multi-call orchestration method (looping over every channel, calling into PlaceTile/DecodeInterleaved/InverseTransformAllChannels/ConvertToBgra/the onDecoded callback) - none is remotely close to the IL-size budget the JIT considers for inlining regardless of EH presence, and CoreCLR's inliner treats 'callee has exception handling regions' as a hard, unconditional block that MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining cannot override (it only raises the JIT's size/complexity budget for otherwise-eligible callees, it does not lift structural NEVER-inline gates like EH, recursion, or localloc). Cross-checked against every genuinely hot, tiny leaf method actually on the profiled call path (BitStream's bit-twiddling helpers, PgfMacroBlock.SetBitAtPos/SetSign/FindNextSignificant, PgfColorConversion.Clamp8): none of them contain a try/catch at all.
part1_tryCatchAudit.conclusion: No live optimization opportunity here. The only EH regions in this codebase sit in methods that would never be inlining candidates by size alone, and none of the actual hot leaf methods have EH to remove in the first place. Restructuring try/catch placement would not change any inlining decision in the current code. Not implemented - there was nothing safe and applicable to change.

part2_aggressiveInliningExperiment.change: Added [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to PgfColorConversion.Clamp8 (called up to 4x per pixel in DecodeYuvaToBgra and every other GetBitmap-family conversion) and PgfMacroBlock.SetBitAtPos/SetSign (called once per newly-significant coefficient in BitplaneDecode) - three small, hot leaf methods that lacked the attribute, unlike BitStream's bit-primitive helpers which already all carry it uniformly.
part2_aggressiveInliningExperiment.correctness: Full codec suite 1393/1393 (one transient failure on a rerun immediately after two backgrounded benchmark processes had just finished was not reproducible on a clean rerun - resource contention, not a real regression) and Browser/WASM build green.
part2_aggressiveInliningExperiment.methodology: Two independent matched-conditions comparisons, each via git stash push/pop isolating just the two changed files, before/after MediumRun (N=15, LaunchCount=2) run back-to-back on the same machine.
part2_aggressiveInliningExperiment.trial1: DecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(False) 121.6ms -> 121.1ms (-0.4%); ProgressiveDecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(False) 135.0ms -> 133.1ms (-1.4%); DecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(True) 138.8ms -> 137.5ms (-0.9%); ProgressiveDecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(True) 149.1ms -> 148.4ms (-0.5%). All four rows improved.
part2_aggressiveInliningExperiment.trial2: DecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(False) 120.5ms -> 122.6ms (+1.7%); ProgressiveDecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(False) 132.5ms -> 132.6ms (+0.1%); DecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(True) 137.5ms -> 138.6ms (+0.8%); ProgressiveDecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(True) 149.7ms -> 148.3ms (-0.9%). Three of four rows regressed.
part2_aggressiveInliningExperiment.result: INCONCLUSIVE - not a provable improvement. Trial 1's uniformly-negative (improving) result did not replicate in trial 2, which was uniformly positive or flat on 3 of 4 rows. Combined across both trials: 5 of 8 row-comparisons improved, 3 regressed, every single delta under 2%. This is the signature of correlated session-level noise (e.g. transient system load affecting all four rows of one trial in the same direction) rather than a real, reproducible per-change effect - the same failure mode this session's methodology notes deliberately guard against by never trusting one matched pair alone. Plausible root cause: Clamp8/SetBitAtPos/SetSign are all small enough (a handful of IL instructions) that RyuJIT's default inlining heuristics likely already inline them at their call sites without the attribute, at least at the Tier1 (fully-optimized) code the MediumRun's warmup reaches - AggressiveInlining mainly matters for Tier0/quick-JIT or borderline-sized methods, neither of which applies here. Reverted (git checkout --); PgfColorConversion.cs and PgfMacroBlock.cs are unchanged from 7748dfa. Do not re-attempt this specific change without either evidence the JIT was NOT already inlining these call sites (e.g. a disassembly diagnoser diff showing an actual call instruction disappearing) or a benchmark methodology that can resolve effects smaller than the ~1-2% noise floor observed on this machine.
